Consider the rectangular region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,2\le u\le 3,\,\,\frac{2\pi }{3}\le v\le \frac{5\pi }{6}},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v).
$$

Find the image of $Δ$ under the action of $T.$
worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we transform each side of $Δ$ separately:

- Consider the image of the bottom side, where we have $v=\frac{2\pi }{3}$ and $2\le u\le 3.$ 

Substituting $v=\frac{2\pi }{3}$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y)=(u\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}),\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3})).\end{aligned}
$$

This line segment makes an angle of $\frac{2\pi }{3}$ with the positive $x$-axis in the $xy$-plane. Moreover, this segment lies on a line that passes through the origin, and its endpoints lie on the circles of radii $2$ and $3$ centered at $O.$

- Consider the image of the top side, where we have $v=\frac{5\pi }{6}$ and $2\le u\le 3.$ 

Substituting $v=\frac{5\pi }{6}$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y)=(u\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{6}),\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{6})).\end{aligned}
$$

This line segment makes an angle of $\frac{5\pi }{6}$ with the positive $x$-axis in the $xy$-plane. Moreover, this segment lies on a line that passes through the origin, and its endpoints lie on the circles of radii $2$ and $3$ centered at $O.$

- Consider the image of the left side, where we have $u=2$ and $\frac{2\pi }{3}\le v\le \frac{5\pi }{6}.$ 

Substituting $u=2$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y)=(2\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡v).\end{aligned}
$$

This is an arc of the circle of radius $2$ centered at the origin in the $xy$-plane. The arc lies in the first quadrant between the polar rays $\theta =\frac{2\pi }{3}$ and $\theta =\frac{5\pi }{6}.$

- Consider the image of the right side, where we have $u=3$ and $\frac{2\pi }{3}\le v\le \frac{5\pi }{6}.$ 

Substituting $u=3$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y)=(3\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,3\operatorname{sin}⁡v).\end{aligned}
$$

This is an arc of the circle of radius $3$ centered at the origin in the $xy$-plane. The arc lies in the first quadrant between the polar rays $\theta =\frac{2\pi }{3}$ and $\theta =\frac{5\pi }{6}.$

Therefore, the image $D$ of $Δ$ under the action of $T$ is the region that is enclosed between 

- two circles with polar equations $r=2$ and $r=3,$ and

- two rays with polar equations $\theta =\frac{2\pi }{3}$ and $\theta =\frac{5\pi }{6},$
